items_missed: No agenda statement - opened with 'is now a good time to talk?' and went straight into inventory. Never laid out the roadmap (gather details, then pricing), never gave the 10-15 minute timeframe, never asked 'sound good?'
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any opening warmth question
Never got the origin address, the destination address, or either zip code - he quoted, priced, and BOOKED a two-truck move without knowing where it starts or ends
Never confirmed the move date. He closed the booking and then said out loud 'take the payment after the move on Saturday or on a Friday' - the rep himself did not know which day he had just booked
No stairs or floors probe at either location, on a move with marble-top dressers, antique mirrors and heavy furniture
No access-concerns probe - parking, truck access, walk distance, HOA or gate restrictions - for two trucks
No additional-stops or storage-stops question
No special-considerations probe - long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns

No moving-stressor question. The customer opened by saying 'I'm getting a divorce' and Jack answered with four consecutive 'Okay's and 'For sure. Okay, that helps.' The single clearest emotional cue on the call went completely unacknowledged
No 'pricing is super simple' opener

No No Worries Damage Coverage - zero mention of the $2,000 accidental-damage coverage and zero mention of the 60 cents/lb baseline, on a call where the customer volunteered antiques, marble tops and 'large antique heavy mirrors.' This is the most damage-exposed call imaginable and insurance never came up
No On-Time Guarantee. He set an 8:30 AM start and promised a morning-of call, but never said we start discounting immediately if we miss the window
Never said truck, gas or insurance are included in the rate - he covered wrap, blankets, tools and taxes but left the biggest inclusions out
Clock section half-covered: he explained the clock starts on arrival and stops at delivery, but never gave the 2.5 hour minimum or the 15-minute prorated increments

Estimate looks light for the job described - 4 movers and 2 trucks at 6-7 hours for ~90% of a 2800 sqft home loaded with heavy antiques and marble. He never explained stairs, walk distance, drive time or traffic as variables that push it up, and only ever framed the number as coming DOWN
No equivalents or reference points used to make the time range concrete (school-bus reference or similar)

Save Your Ass only half-delivered - he made the prep-equals-lower-bill point twice ('if you get rid of the couch... all these things are just gonna end up reducing that time'), but never gave a single consolidation example (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls), never gave the take-a-carload tip, and never closed it with 'does that make sense?'

Offered the booking as a fork - 'I can send you this quote now or if you'd like... I can set you up now' - which hands the customer an exit. She booked anyway, but the fork is a habit that will cost him on softer calls
Never explained what is in the confirmation email - no bolded key-details list at the top, no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no hours or how-to-reach-us at the close
Used the customer's name ('Allie') exactly once, in the first sentence, and never again

Real referral moment wasted - she asked 'is it normal for people to use like a separate company for that?' about the baby grand and got 'there's a lot of specialist' with no name, no referral, no follow-up offer
Misheard the customer twice on box volume ('I thought you said we're not moving the whole house but it is packed super tight'), forcing her to re-explain and costing about a minute
top_strength: The rate explanation and the no-hidden-fees pitch were the best part of the call and genuinely well done. He broke the number down the right way - '$420 an hour. So it's $105 per mover, so $420 for the four movers' - then stacked the exclusions cleanly: 'there's no credit card fees, there's no taxes. There's no travel fees. There's no material costs. There's literally no other fees.' He also handled the baby grand disqualification with real integrity, naming it early and unprompted rather than letting it surface on move day, and he justified the 2-truck/4-mover call with reasoning the customer could follow ('if we go with one truck and less people I think it would fill up and be a long day'). Then he asked for the booking and got it in 8.4 minutes.
coaching_note: Jack, this call was one sentence away from a much better score, and it was the same sentence all call: No Worries. Your customer told you she is moving antique marble-top dressers and 'large antique heavy mirrors' and you never once mentioned that we cover up to $2,000 to repair, replace or reimburse accidental damage. Say it right where she lists the antiques: 'That's exactly why I want to mention our No Worries Damage Coverage - we cover up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse anything we accidentally damage, and that's included, not an add-on.' On this call that line is worth more than the whole pricing block, because damage risk is her actual fear. Second priority: you booked a move without an address or a confirmed date, and the customer heard you say 'Saturday or on a Friday' out loud. Lock origin address, destination address, and the date before you ever quote - that is also the root of our estimate-accuracy gap, because you cannot price drive time, walk distance or stairs on an address you do not have. Third, smaller but it matters: she told you she is getting a divorce and you said 'Okay' four times. One line - 'I'm sorry, that's a lot to carry on top of a move. We'll make this part easy on you' - costs you three seconds and changes the whole call. Your closing habit needs one fix too: stop offering 'send the quote OR book it.' Ask for the booking as the single option and back it with no deposit.
phone_presence_notes: Easy, casual and likeable in his word choice ('Too easy. Fantastic', 'Amazing', and a light joke about the washer/dryer that she played along with), but he flatly no-sold her divorce disclosure with four consecutive 'Okay's, used her name only once, misheard her twice, and made the last line about Einstein rather than her ('that helps us get full up on Friday').
